jobs.title: Android Engineer, Growth
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Growth team is responsible for helping millions of users discover the value of ChatGPT and seamlessly access our paid experiences. We build the mobile experiences that drive activation, conversion, and retention across our subscription products.

Our work sits at the intersection of product, design, engineering, and experimentation. We own critical user journeys including upgrade surfaces, purchase experiences, subscription management, and the end-to-end experiences that help users get the most value from ChatGPT.

As an Android Engineer on Growth, you'll help shape how users experience and engage with ChatGPT's paid offerings on one of our most important platforms.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for an Android engineer who enjoys building polished consumer experiences and using data to improve them over time.

You'll develop the mobile surfaces that power subscription growth, including upsells, upgrade prompts, purchase flows, entitlement experiences, and other high-impact product initiatives. You'll collaborate closely with product managers, designers, data scientists, and backend engineers to rapidly experiment, learn from user behavior, and deliver intuitive experiences to millions of users.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of three days per week in the office.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Build and ship high-quality Android features that improve activation, conversion, and retention for ChatGPT's paid offerings.

 - Own end-to-end development of growth initiatives, from technical design through launch and iteration.

 - Develop subscription experiences including paywalls, upgrade prompts, purchase flows, and entitlement management.

 - Partner closely with product, design, and data teams to define hypotheses, run experiments, and measure impact.

 - Use experimentation and user insights to continuously improve the paid user experience.

 - Contribute to the evolution of our Android architecture, tooling, testing practices, and engineering standards.

 - Help maintain a fast, reliable, and delightful mobile experience for millions of users.



You might Thrive in this role if

 - 4+ years of professional software engineering experience, including meaningful Android experience.

 - A track record of shipping and maintaining consumer-facing Android features at scale.

 - Proficiency in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose.

 - Experience integrating backend APIs and building robust client-side architectures.

 - Comfort operating in fast-moving, collaborative environments with product ambiguity.

 - Strong product quality, craftsmanship, communication, and cross-functional collaboration.

 - Experience using data and experimentation to inform decisions and iterate quickly.

 - Bonus: subscription or in-app purchase systems, growth engineering, A/B testing, Google Play Billing, entitlement management, Jetpack Compose, analytics instrumentation, or consumer products at large scale.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, ML Platform
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

SOFTWARE ENGINEER, ML PLATFORM

As a Software Engineer on ML Platform at SpaceXSI, you'll build the infrastructure that turns real product usage into better models, and keeps research moving fast on large GPU fleets. ML Platform is organized into four teams. Depending on your background, you may join any of them. We're looking for strong distributed-systems and infrastructure engineers who want to sit next to research and ship platform primitives that move the product.



RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Design, build, and operate core platform systems used daily by ML researchers and product engineers

 - Partner closely with research to turn recurring pain into durable infrastructure

 - Own reliability, performance, and developer experience for the systems in your lane

 - Ship iteratively in a flat, high-ownership environment. Measure impact, then raise the bar
   
   

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in computer science, machine learning, or another quantitative discipline; OR equivalent work experience

 - 5+ years of industry experience working with production distributed systems (e.g., infrastructure, ingestion, data pipelines, or scheduling/orchestration, etc.)
   
   

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

 - Experience owning production distributed systems at meaningful scale (ingestion, data pipelines, scheduling/orchestration, or similar)

 - Experience partnering and building platforms for ML researchers and product engineers

 - Thrive where ownership is high and the feedback loop is short

 - Telemetry: event ingestion, product analytics pipelines, OpenTelemetry / tracing, reliable data APIs

 - Product Data Platform: data frameworks, Spark / Flink / Ray, ML dataset and training-data infrastructure

 - Observability: experiment / run monitoring, debug and eval tooling, agent-friendly observability UX

 - ML DevX and Systems: GPU / cluster scheduling, job queues, node health, research compute developer experience
   
   

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

 - We're in-person with cozy offices in North Beach, San Francisco, Palo Alto, and Manhattan, New York, complete with well-stocked libraries

 - If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 2-3 short technicals. After, we'll schedule an onsite in our office, where you'll work on a small project, discuss ideas, and meet the team
   
   

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

Annual Salary:

$140,000 - $225,000 USD

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at SpaceXSI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Sentry Software (Manufacturing)
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

The Sentry Tower Software team is responsible for developing robotic systems that provide force protection capabilities, monitoring the perimeter of secure areas, land or sea, for approaching people, vehicles, and vessels. We live in a world where security officers are increasingly overwhelmed by sensor data feeds. Our products leverage advanced sensor fusion and autonomy to seamlessly render activity in the environment to Lattice's common operating picture.

About the Job

We are looking for a Software Engineer with a focus in Manufacturing to join our rapidly growing team in Costa Mesa. In this role you will be responsible for building and maintaining software for current and next generation Sentry Tower systems. You will be responsible for developing automated test suites and user-friendly interfaces to streamline hardware verification and issue diagnosis for non-technical users. You will implement robust error-capturing mechanisms that provide actionable insights for efficient troubleshooting and quality assurance.

Every tower we ship passes through this software. It is what proves a unit works before it leaves the floor, which makes it the last chance to catch a defect while the hardware is still in reach and the fix costs an hour instead of a trip to a site. A test that passes when it should not have is the most expensive kind of bug we have, because it ships.

The honest version: your users are technicians on a production floor, not engineers, and their time is the constraint. That means a lot of the work is unglamorous by design: clear error messages, tooling that fails in an obvious way, and diagnostics a person can follow at 6am without calling you. You will also be pulled into whatever is blocking the line, which does not wait for your sprint. The upside is a feedback loop most software engineers never get, since the people using what you built are in the same building and will tell you within a day.

Our Product: https://www.anduril.com/hardware/sentry/

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Develop automated test suites to verify hardware functionality and performance.

- Create user-friendly interfaces to facilitate issue diagnosis for non-technical users.

- Implement robust error-capturing mechanisms to provide actionable insights.

- Collaborate with hardware and quality assurance teams to ensure seamless integration of testing tools.

- Work directly with the technicians and manufacturing engineers who use your tooling every shift, and treat their time as the thing you are optimizing.

- Continuously improve testing frameworks to enhance efficiency and reliability.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Experience building test automation, instrumentation, or tooling for hardware, and comfort working on a bench with the hardware in front of you.

- Proficiency in Python for test and tooling work, plus 2+ years in Rust or C++ to work in the services under test.

- Solid grasp of networking principles, including CAN and Ethernet protocols, along with expertise in hardware interfacing, diagnostic tools (e.g., Wireshark, CANoe), and cybersecurity principles as they pertain to secure and reliable sensor data transmission.

- Strong engineering background from industry or school, ideally in areas/fields such as Computer Science, Software Engineering, Mathematics, or Physics.

- US person status required, with eligibility to obtain and maintain a US security clearance.

US Salary Range

$220,000—$292,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

-

No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

- Please always verify communications:

- Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

- Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

-

Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

-

What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. The Sentry Tower Software team develops robotic systems that provide force protection capabilities, monitoring the perimeter of secure areas, land or sea, for approaching people, vehicles, and vessels. We live in a world where security officers are increasingly overwhelmed by sensor data feeds. Our products leverage advanced sensor fusion and autonomy to seamlessly render activity in the environment to Lattice's common operating picture.

About the Job

Not every Sentry Tower does the same job. The same core platform that watches a perimeter for people and vehicles also underpins our ground-based air defense variants, where the tower's mission is detecting and tracking aircraft, and the sensor payload, the radar integration, and the configuration all shift accordingly. We're hiring a Software Engineer to develop and own the software for those variants, funded by and delivered to our Air Defense program. The threat they exist for is the cheap, fast, hard-to-see aircraft that has changed what defending a fixed site means. Detection has to happen with enough time left to do something about it, which puts the burden on how well the payload, the tracking, and the configuration actually work together on a real tower.

You will work in the same declarative NixOS platform the rest of the team builds on, owning your variants' slice of it: product configuration, radar and camera payload integration, networking, manufacturing test hooks, and the software update path. Some of this is new feature work driven by program requirements, and some of it is consolidation, because these variant configurations grew up separately from our modern platform base, and moving them onto it means understanding both well enough to prove nothing was lost in the move. This program delivers several products, a few of them tower variants, and those variants are what you'll work on. The result is that you end up knowing how they are put together better than anyone, which is genuinely useful to a team this size.

This is a good role for an engineer who wants breadth. You'll touch the radar and camera services, the network configuration, the build system, and the manufacturing and field tooling, with an experienced team around you owning each of those domains in depth. Travel is light, roughly 10% and mostly local, to test sites and the manufacturing floor rather than overseas.

The honest shape of the role: the scope is the program's tower variants rather than the whole product line, and the schedule comes substantially from the contract rather than from what you would pick next. Most days are integration work, configuration, and support rather than novel algorithms. What you get in exchange is unusual breadth and products you own end to end. If you want to go deep on one technical specialty, this is not that role.

Our Product: https://www.anduril.com/sentry

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own the software configuration for the Air Defense tower variants: product definitions, payload and sensor configuration, networking, and image builds in our declarative platform.

- Integrate and support the variants' sensor payloads, particularly radar and infrared camera services, including the configuration and behavior differences that separate them from our perimeter security products.

- Develop features driven by Air Defense program requirements, working from program needs through design, implementation, and delivery into a shipping product.

- Migrate the variants' legacy configuration onto our modern platform base, replacing product-specific one-offs with the common, composable modules the rest of the fleet uses.

- Own the variants' software update and deployment path, and the manufacturing test configuration that validates units as they're built.

- Support the product in the field and on the line: triage issues, reproduce and root-cause them, fix what's yours, and drive what isn't with the owning team.

- Work with the Air Defense program's engineers and stakeholders to keep requirements, schedule, and technical reality aligned.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- 2+ years of professional software engineering building and shipping real systems.

- Proficiency in Rust or C++, with the ability to work across an existing codebase you didn't write.

- Solid Linux systems fundamentals: the command line, systemd, networking basics, and log-driven debugging.

- Practical experience integrating software with hardware, whether sensors, embedded devices, or instrumentation, and comfort working on a bench with real equipment.

- Demonstrated ability to own a piece of a larger system end to end, including the unglamorous parts: configuration, deployment, testing, and support.

- Clear written communication, since you'll be the interface between a program's requirements and the team's implementation.

- US person status required, with eligibility to obtain and maintain a US security clearance.

NICE TO HAVE

- Experience with radar, RF systems, or air surveillance and tracking.

- Experience with camera or imaging pipelines, especially infrared.

- Experience with declarative configuration management or infrastructure-as-code. Nix or NixOS is what we use; adjacent tooling is a fine starting point.

- Python for tooling, scripting, and test automation.

- Robotics experience, or work with motion control and pointing systems.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Sentry Software (Allied Customer Deployment)
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

The Sentry Tower Software team develops robotic systems that provide force protection capabilities, monitoring the perimeter of secure areas, land or sea, for approaching people, vehicles, and vessels. We live in a world where security officers are increasingly overwhelmed by sensor data feeds. Our products leverage advanced sensor fusion and autonomy to seamlessly render activity in the environment to Lattice's common operating picture.

About the Job

Sentry Towers protect perimeters for allied partner nations as well as US customers, and those deployments are their own engineering problem. A partner program brings its own site conditions, its own communications and network environment, its own integration requirements, and its own operators, and none of it is solved by shipping the standard configuration and hoping. We're hiring a Software Engineer dedicated to one such program: making our towers work for that customer, in their environment, and keeping them working. This is a customer with no second system to fall back on. When a tower is down, the perimeter it was watching is being watched by people instead, and the fix depends on an engineer who understands both our software and their site.

This is a hands-on integration and support role rather than a pure feature-development one. You will own the software configuration for this program's towers, built on our declarative NixOS platform: product configuration, network integration into the customer's environment, payload and sensor setup, and the deployment and update path for systems in the customer's hands. When something doesn't work in the field, you're the engineer who reproduces it, root-causes it, and either fixes it or drives the fix with the team that owns the component.

Expect meaningful travel, roughly 30% of your time, much of it extended international trips for installation, integration, and operator support. Some of it is not optional: when a program milestone depends on being on site, you'll be on site. The compensation for that is direct contact with the people using what you build. You will watch an operator use your work, learn things no bug report would have told you, and carry them back.

Worth weighing honestly before you apply. This is reactive work by nature: your week can get reorganized by what broke, and the roadmap you planned on Monday is not always the one you follow. You will go deep on one program rather than broad across the product, which builds unusually specific expertise and means your work is harder to point at than a shipped feature. Time zones will cost you: some of the coordination happens early, some late, and it is not evenly distributed. People take this role and love it, and people take it and find out they wanted to be writing features. Both are worth knowing about yourself first.

Our Product: https://www.anduril.com/sentry

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own the software configuration for this program's tower variants in our declarative platform, from product definitions through payload and sensor configuration to image builds.

- Integrate towers into the customer's network and communications environment, covering addressing, routing, backhaul, and any interfaces the program requires.

- Own the deployment and software update path for the program's fielded systems, including provisioning, staged rollout, and verification that an update landed cleanly.

- Travel to customer sites for installation, integration, commissioning, and operator support, including extended international deployments, at approximately 30% of your time.

- Be the program's technical front line: triage field issues, reproduce them on a bench or in simulation, root-cause them, and either fix them directly or drive the fix with the owning team.

- Build the tooling, documentation, and runbooks that let field personnel and the customer's own operators resolve routine problems without escalating.

- Represent the program back into engineering, making sure customer requirements and field realities reach the teams whose roadmaps need to reflect them.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- 2+ years of professional software engineering, with time spent on systems that are deployed and operated rather than only developed.

- Solid Linux systems skills: the command line, systemd, log analysis, and the ability to diagnose a misbehaving service on a machine you didn't set up.

- Practical networking competence: addressing and subnetting, routing, DNS, VLANs, and packet capture, enough to integrate a system into someone else's network and debug it when it doesn't come up.

- Proficiency in at least one of Python, Rust, C++, or Go, and willingness to work in Rust and C++ where our services live.

- Willingness and ability to travel approximately 30% of the time, including extended international trips that cannot be rescheduled around, and to work effectively on customer sites.

- Strong written communication and follow-through, since much of this role is coordinating across time zones and leaving behind documentation someone else depends on.

About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About the Role:

We’re hiring seasoned engineers to join our teams that work on the financial backbone of Gusto's money movement — the ledger, reconciliation, and reporting systems that account for every dollar, and the payment profile that determines how employers fund payroll and how employees and contractors get paid. As a Gusto Software Engineer at this level, you’ll be guiding projects end-to-end by driving large technical architectural decisions (focusing on scale and modularity), understanding how to take existing systems closer to desired end states, executing on projects, and maintaining code that powers core experiences. If you’re interested in building elegant software with far-reaching effects in our modern economy, join us!

About the Team:

Financial Data & Payment Profile (FDPP) sits inside Gusto's Payments organization, which moves money safely between partners, employers, employees, government authorities, and Gusto. FDPP owns the two things that every one of those movements depends on.

Financial Data is the system of record for the money itself: the ledger and subledger behind every payment, the reconciliation that proves our books agree with our banks and partners, the investigation of the variances that surface when they do not, and the financial reporting that Accounting, Finance, and Compliance depend on. When Gusto needs to answer where a dollar is — and prove it — the answer comes from systems this team builds.

Payment Profile is what makes a payment possible in the first place: the payment methods available to a customer, the bank accounts and connections behind them, the verification that makes those accounts trustworthy, and the profile state that decides whether a payment can happen at all. Hundreds of thousands of businesses depend on this being right the first time — and on it recovering gracefully when a bank account, a connection, or a preference changes.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

- Design, build, and test the financial data systems that record every dollar Gusto moves — the ledger and subledger that serve as the system of record, the transaction models underneath them, and the financial reporting that Accounting, Finance, Compliance, and our partners rely on to close the books

- Build reconciliation at Gusto's scale: prove that our internal records agree with bank, processor, and partner statements, and make the breaks that fall out of that comparison traceable rather than mysterious

- Lead variance investigation end-to-end — the tooling, instrumentation, and runbooks that turn "the numbers don't tie" into a specific root cause, and then into a fix that eliminates the whole class of break

- Own the payment profile: how employers are set up to fund payroll and how employees and contractors are set up to be paid — the payment methods available and the rules that govern which apply to whom, the bank accounts and connections behind them, and the verification state that determines whether money can move at all

- Make setup and verification something a small business can finish on its own — instant bank verification, graceful handling of broken or revoked connections, and a clear path back to a payable state when something changes

- Help scale one of the largest Ruby/Rails and TypeScript/React applications in the world

- Collaborate on complex and ambiguous problems with partnerships from Engineering, Product Management, Design, Data Science, Accounting, Finance, Compliance, Operations, and other cross-functional teams

- Mentor and grow fellow engineers working to create holistic and scalable solutions

Here’s what we're looking for:

- Successful applicants have at least 10+ years of experience and the enthusiasm for a collaborative, test-driven environment

- Experience building fault-tolerant, mission-critical software as well as designing and developing robust, distributed systems using multiple general-purpose programming languages

- Experience influencing and guiding the work of multiple teams on scaling, refactoring, and optimizing legacy products

- Experience architecting, building, and testing large-scale production level code that is maintainable, structured, and well-documented

- An aptitude and interest in bringing clarity and simplicity to complex and ambiguous problems

- Ability to communicate technical complexity and help facilitate informed tradeoffs

- Experience in one or more of these domains is strongly preferred: ledger or subledger design, financial reconciliation, accounting systems, or payments infrastructure

- Comfort with double-entry accounting concepts — journal entries, chart of accounts, debits and credits, and tying a subledger out to the general ledger — and the ability to work with accountants and controllers in their own vocabulary

- Experience building systems where correctness, auditability, and immutability matter more than raw throughput, and where a silent data error is worse than an outage

- Bonus: Experience with bank account verification, payment rails (ACH, wire, RTP), or third-party banking data and verification providers

- Bonus: Experience with Ruby on Rails, Typescript, and React

Our cash compensation amount for this role is targeted at $183,000-$200,000 /yr in Denver & most remote locations, and $222,000-$245,000 /yr for San Francisco, Seattle & New York. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including candidate experience and expertise, and may vary from the amounts listed above.

At Gusto, we don't use titles the traditional way, as a signal of rank or hierarchy. Instead, our titles describe two things at once — your craft (what you do, e.g. Engineering, Design) and your scope of ownership (what you're accountable for) — which is why you'll see something like "Head of X" instead of a rank word like "Director" that tells you neither. Because of this, the title on this posting may look different from what you'd expect based on the scope and seniority of the role, and from how similar roles are typically titled elsewhere. If you have questions about how this role compares to your current title or level, your recruiter can help translate.

Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. Employees who are based in those locations will be expected to work from the office on designated days approximately 2-3 days per week (or more depending on role). The same office expectations apply to all Symmetry roles, Gusto's subsidiary, whose physical office is in Scottsdale.

Note: The San Francisco office expectations encompass both the San Francisco and San Jose metro areas.

When approved to work from a location other than a Gusto office, a secure, reliable, and consistent internet connection is required. This includes non-office days for hybrid employees.

Reliable, consistent presence: We expect regular and predictable attendance, whether you're working in-office, hybrid, or fully remote, so that you stay closely connected to your team, customers, and stakeholders in real time and ensure colleagues and customers receive the timely support and responsiveness they deserve.

Our customers come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, not just because it's the right thing to do, but because it makes our company stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for small businesses, you will find a home at Gusto.

Gusto is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. Gusto considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Gusto is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. We want to see our candidates perform to the best of their ability. If you require a medical or religious accommodation at any time throughout your candidate journey, please fill out this form and a member of our team will get in touch with you.

Gusto takes security and protection of your personal information very seriously. Please review our Fraudulent Activity Disclaimer.

Personal information collected and processed as part of your Gusto application will be subject to Gusto's Applicant Privacy Notice.

Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase, we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase.

This is a unique opportunity to reimagine and implement how Coinbase interfaces with high throughput blockchains, serving millions of daily users. The Wallets team enables Coinbase users globally to interface with 50+ blockchains. Our backend systems have already powered billions of crypto addresses and requests. Our team is continuing to develop new ways to scale for the next billion.

At a high level, our team owns the set of services that powers all of the sends and receives for Coinbase's custodial products. These distributed backend systems help construct, sign, broadcast, and ingest onchain transactions. Come work with a team of brilliant and passionate engineers on building the next generation of Wallet products!

What you'll do:

- Design, develop, and maintain the future of our wallet systems

- Collaborate with teams across the company on integrations with our services

- Participate in code reviews and provide constructive feedback to maintain high code quality standards

- Troubleshoot and debug complicated problems

Required Skills and Experience:

- You have at least 2+ years of experience in software engineering

- Familiarity with GoLang and/or Ruby is a plus

- You’ve designed, built, scaled and maintained production services, and know how to compose a service oriented architecture

- Experience with decomposing large software systems is a plus

- Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work closely with other team members and stakeholders

- You have a strong attention to detail

- You’re passionate about building an open financial system that brings the world together

- You take ownership of well-scoped problems from investigation through implementation, rollout, and production support

Pay Transparency Notice: Base salary varies by location (see range below). Total compensation may also include equity and bonus eligibility, and benefits (medical, dental, vision, 401(k)).

Annual base salary range (excluding equity and bonus):

$152,405—$179,300 USD

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information. Applicants with criminal histories will be considered consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

- US Applicants: View Employee Rights, Know Your Rights, and E-Verify Notice of Participation.

jobs.title: Full Stack Software Engineer, Internal Platforms
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

FULL STACK SOFTWARE ENGINEER, INTERNAL PLATFORMS

The application software team is the central nervous system of SpaceX – we create mission critical applications that are used throughout SpaceX to accelerate launch vehicle production and flight as well as systems that allow Starlink to grow into a worldwide fast, reliable Internet service. We are looking for engineers who treat fellow teammates with fairness, respect, and support.

Our team is currently creating and evolving systems to enable rapid build and reuse of Starship as well as designing the next generation manufacturing software that will be used in high throughput factories for Starlink. Other applications range from platforms that support concurrent streams of data from many always-on assets to manage the world’s largest satellite constellation to public facing systems where customers can join our Starlink network globally. We work closely with engineers throughout the company to create and update our systems with respect to crewed launches, Starship flights, changes to the Starlink network and much more.

Aerospace experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, respectful, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on a super inspiring mission. You will have full ownership of challenging problems, working with a team of enthusiastic engineers with diverse perspectives to design and produce solutions that enable SpaceX to move towards our goals at a rapid pace. The success of the missions at SpaceX depends on the software that you and your team produce.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

- Develop highly reliable software solutions that are used across SpaceX

- Create new applications that improve how SpaceX operates

- Build prototypes to prove out key design concepts and quantify technical constraints

- Own all aspects of software engineering and product development

- Deep dive into your users’ problems to find and create efficient solutions

- Bring your voice to the table in team collaborations on architecture, design, and code reviews

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

- Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, math, or scientific discipline; OR 2+ years of professional experience building software in lieu of a degree

- 1+ years of experience in full stack development

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

- Programming experience in Python, C#.NET, Go, Scala, Java, or similar object-oriented language

- 1+ years of rigorous experience building single page web applications

- Experience with version control, continuous integration, and continuous delivery concepts

- Expertise in designing software systems

- Deep understanding of testing, continuous integration, build, deployment & monitoring

- Expertise in profiling and improving application performance

- Experience with build systems (Make, Bazel/Pants/Buck, Gradle) and package management tools (pip, npm)

- Experience with UNIX-like operating systems and tools like Terraform, Ansible, Puppet for managing them

- Experience working with in-stream data processing using Apache Kafka, RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ, or similar technologies

- Production experience with Docker and Kubernetes

- Front-end experience in Angular, React, or similar JavaScript framework

- Database experience with PostgreSQL, SQL Server, or similar database technologies

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

- You may be asked to work extended hours/weekends dependent on launch cadence

- This role requires you to be onsite. Remote and/or hybrid work will not be considered

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 1: $125,000.00 - $160,000.00
Level 2: $145,000.00 - $195,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

- To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Research Engineer, Cybersecurity RL
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
locations: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About Horizons

The Horizons team leads Anthropic's reinforcement learning (RL) research and development, playing a critical role in advancing our AI systems. We've contributed to every Claude release, with significant impact on the autonomy, coding, and reasoning capabilities of Anthropic's models.

About the role

We're hiring for the Cybersecurity RL team within Horizons. As a Research Engineer, you'll help to safely advance the capabilities of our models in secure coding, vulnerability remediation, and other areas of defensive cybersecurity.

This role blends research and engineering, requiring you to both develop novel approaches and realize them in code. Your work will include designing and implementing RL environments, conducting experiments and evaluations, delivering your work into production training runs, and collaborating with other researchers, engineers, and cybersecurity specialists across and outside Anthropic.

The role requires domain expertise in cybersecurity paired with interest or experience in training safe AI models. For example, you might be a white hat hacker who's curious about how LLMs could augment or transform your work, a security engineer interested in how AI could help harden systems at scale, or a detection and response professional wondering how models could enhance defensive workflows.

You may be a good fit if you:

-

Have experience in cybersecurity research.

-

Have experience with machine learning.

-

Have strong software engineering skills.

-

Can balance research exploration with engineering implementation.

-

Are passionate about AI's potential and committed to developing safe and beneficial systems.

Strong candidates may also have:

-

Professional experience in security engineering, fuzzing, detection and response, or other applied defensive work.

-

Experience participating in or building CTF competitions and cyber ranges.

-

Academic research experience in cybersecurity.

-

Familiarity with RL techniques and environments.

-

Familiarity with LLM training methodologies.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$500,000—$850,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Security Engineer
jobs.description:
About Mixpanel

Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com.

About the Role

Mixpanel's Information Security & Risk Management (ISRM) team is hiring a Security Engineer to run the day-to-day work of our security operations: vulnerability management, detection and monitoring, and incident response. You'll work closely with engineering teams to find and close real risk, tune our detections so every alert is worth investigating, and use AI to make triage and investigation faster. This is a hands-on role for an engineer early to mid-way in their career, with a defined path to Senior Security Engineer.

Responsibilities

- Vulnerability management: Triage findings from vulnerability scanners, penetration tests, bug bounty reports, and dependency tooling. Validate exploitability and impact in our environment, and assign severity accordingly.

- Remediation with engineering: Work with engineering teams to agree on fixes and timelines, track each vulnerability through to closure within SLA, and escalate items at risk of missing it.

- Detection and monitoring: Build, tune, and maintain detections in our SIEM across cloud, identity, endpoint, and application logs, and cut false positives so on-call time goes to real threats.

- AI-assisted security operations: Use AI tools (e.g. Claude Code) to speed up alert triage, enrich investigations, write and test detection logic, and automate repetitive SecOps work.

- Incident response: Investigate and respond to security incidents from first alert through containment, eradication, and recovery, and write clear post-incident reviews with follow-up actions.

- Coverage and runbooks: Identify gaps in log sources and detection coverage, onboard new sources, and keep runbooks current so the team responds consistently.

- On-call: Take part in the security on-call rotation.

We're Looking For Someone With

- 3-5 years of experience in security engineering, security operations, detection and response, or a related role

- Hands-on vulnerability management experience, including triaging and validating scanner and pentest findings and working with engineers to remediate them

- Experience working in a SIEM (e.g. Splunk, Google SecOps/Chronicle, Panther, Elastic), including writing queries and building or tuning detections

- Experience investigating and responding to security incidents

- Understanding of common attack techniques and how to detect them, for example using MITRE ATT&CK

- Working knowledge of cloud security in GCP or AWS, including IAM, audit logging, and common misconfigurations

- Scripting skills in Python, Go, or a similar language to automate tasks and work with log data

- Hands-on experience using AI tools (e.g. Claude Code) to automate security workflows, or a strong interest in building that skill

- Sound judgment on severity and risk, including knowing when to escalate and when an issue can wait

- Ability to explain security issues clearly to engineers and get fixes prioritized without slowing teams down unnecessarily

- Strong written communication and follow-through, with the ability to manage many concurrent items and work independently

Nice to Have

- Experience with detection-as-code (e.g. Sigma rules, version-controlled detections with CI testing)

- Experience with EDR tools (e.g. CrowdStrike, SentinelOne)

- Experience with SOAR or workflow automation platforms (e.g. Tines, Torq)

- Experience with Kubernetes and container security

- Experience running or supporting a bug bounty program

- GCIH, GCIA, GCFA, OSCP, or similar certification

What Success Looks Like

- First 3 months: You understand our environment, log sources, and vulnerability pipeline, triage incoming findings and alerts on your own, and have joined the on-call rotation.

- By 6 months: You own the vulnerability triage queue end-to-end, have tuned our noisiest detections to reduce false positives, and have led the response to incidents.

- By 12 months: You've shipped at least one AI-assisted workflow that measurably reduces triage or investigation time, added detections for coverage gaps you identified, and are taking on larger projects as you grow toward Senior Security Engineer.

Growth Path

This role is part of a defined security engineering career path. As you build experience, you can grow into Senior Security Engineer, where you'll set the direction of our detection and response program, lead complex incidents, and design security improvements with engineering teams.

Compensation

The amount listed below is the total target cash compensation (TTCC) and includes base compensation and variable compensation in the form of either a company bonus or commissions. Variable compensation type is determined by your role and level. In addition to the cash compensation provided, this position is also eligible for equity consideration and other benefits including medical, vision, and dental insurance coverage. You can view our benefits offerings here.

Our salary ranges are determined by role and level and are benchmarked to the SF Bay Area Technology data cut released by Radford, a global compensation database. The range displayed represents the minimum and maximum TTCC for new hire salaries for the position across all of our US locations. To stay on top of market conditions, we refresh our salary ranges twice a year so these ranges may change in the future. Within the range, individual pay is determined by experience, job-related skills, qualifications, and other factors. If you have questions about the specific range, your recruiter can share this information.

Mixpanel Compensation Range

$160,000—$210,000 USD

Benefits and Perks

- Comprehensive Medical, Vision, and Dental Care

- Mental Wellness Benefit

- Generous Vacation Policy & Additional Company Holidays

- Enhanced Parental Leave

- Volunteer Time Off

- Additional US Benefits: Pre-Tax Benefits including 401(K), Wellness Benefit, Holiday Break

*please note that benefits and perks for contract positions will vary*

Culture Values

- Make Bold Bets: We choose courageous action over comfortable progress.

- Innovate with Insight: We tackle decisions with rigor and judgment - combining data, experience and collective wisdom to drive powerful outcomes.

- One Team: We collaborate across boundaries to achieve far greater impact than any of us could accomplish alone.

- Candor with Connection: We build meaningful relationships that enable honest feedback and direct conversations.

- Champion the Customer: We seek to deeply understand our customers’ needs, ensuring their success is our north star.

- Powerful Simplicity: We find elegant solutions to complex problems, making sophisticated things accessible.

Why choose Mixpanel?

We’re a leader in analytics with over 29,000 customers and $277M invested from prominent investors: like Andreessen-Horowitz, Sequoia, YC, and, most recently, Bain Capital. Mixpanel’s pioneering event-based data analytics platform offers a powerful yet simple solution for companies to understand user behaviors and easily track overarching company success metrics. Our accomplished teams continuously facilitate our expansion by tackling the ever-evolving challenges tied to scaling, reliability, design, and service. Choosing to work at Mixpanel means you’ll be helping the world’s most innovative companies learn from their data so they can make better decisions.

Mixpanel is an equal opportunity employer supporting workforce diversity. At Mixpanel, we are focused on things that really matter—our people, our customers, our partners—out of a recognition that those relationships are the most valuable assets we have. We actively encourage women, people with disabilities, veterans, underrepresented minorities, and LGBTQ+ people to apply. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance or other similar laws that may be applicable, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We’ve immersed ourselves in our Culture and Values as our guiding principles for the impact we want to have and the future we are building.

jobs.title: Applied AI Engineer, Enterprise - EDU
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Across industries, OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering (AIE) team helps organizations turn frontier AI into safe, reliable production systems that deliver meaningful business outcomes. We work directly with customers’ engineering, product, security, and transformation teams to navigate complex architectures, data environments, governance requirements, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better OpenAI products and reusable patterns that help customers move faster.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As an Enterprise AIE, you will serve as a technical partner to leading organizations including universities and other educational institutions, helping them turn ambitious AI use cases into durable production systems and adoption at scale. You will combine deep technical judgment with hands-on engineering to provide technical leadership on complex customer deployments. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions about model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by durable production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful business impact. Your deployment experience will also directly influence how OpenAI’s products evolve.

This role may be based in one of our offices in New York City or San Francisco, or it may be performed remotely. Office-based employees follow a hybrid work model with three days per week in the office. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Work hands-on in code to design, build, evaluate, and deploy AI systems from prototype to reliable production and scaled adoption that solve important customer problems and deliver measurable business outcomes.

 - Partner with enterprise customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and success criteria.

 - Make sound technical decisions across model selection, agent and tool design, retrieval, context design, data pipelines, evaluation, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.

 - Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers to resolution.

 - Partner closely with customers’ engineering teams and OpenAI’s Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and Go-to-Market teams to turn deployment experience into actionable product feedback.

 - Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.
   
   


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - Have personally designed, built, and shipped AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, taking them from prototype to production and making substantial contributions through coding, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or production engineering. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting.

 - Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working end to end across model APIs, agent and tool development, retrieval and data pipelines, evaluation, observability, integrations, and production operations. Experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.

 - Know how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, automated graders, production signals, and human judgment.

 - Have navigated enterprise production requirements, including integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.

 - Experience navigating education or research environments, including institutional data, privacy, access controls and complex integrations, is valuable.

 - Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.

 - Communicate clearly and credibly with hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security and product teams, and executives.

 - Take end-to-end ownership, exercise strong technical judgment, and move effectively through ambiguity.

 - Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility. Experience working with education institutions, particularly universities, is preferred but not required. Prior OpenAI product experience is not required.





About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. 

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

jobs.title: Security & IT Operations Engineer
jobs.description:
About Prefect

Prefect builds automation for an unpredictable world. The last decade of automation was about protecting workflows from unpredictability; in the agentic era, unpredictability is the point. Our mission is to give people confidence in automated work, whether that work is a mission-critical data pipeline or a fleet of AI agents.

In August 2026, Prefect and Dagster, competitors for eight years, joined forces to build the next generation of automation infrastructure. Today, our ecosystem includes Dagster, the data platform; Prefect, the agent platform; and FastMCP, the leading open-source developer framework for the MCP ecosystem. Together, our open-source and commercial products are trusted by Fortune 500 companies, data innovators, and high-growth technology companies around the world.

We think of our culture as the operating system of the company. We’ve carefully created a supportive, high-performance environment that empowers our team to do the best work of their careers, have meaningful impact, and continue growing personally and professionally. We’re a remote-first team that values high standards, ownership, and thoughtful collaboration.




THE ROLE

In August, Dagster and Prefect became one company. Behind the scenes, that left us with two of nearly everything: two SOC 2 programs, two ways of managing laptops, overlapping tools and accounts, and a long list of tools that each need one clear owner. We're hiring a Security & IT Operations Engineer to turn all of it into one setup that runs well and gets easier to run every quarter.

You'll own the day-to-day of our security compliance program and our corporate IT. You'll report to our Security & Systems Lead as the first hire on this new team.

Our customers are enterprise data, infrastructure, ML and AI teams, and our products run code inside their data infrastructure. AI has made attacks cheap and fast, so customers look hard at how we protect them, and a well-run security and compliance program is a big part of our answer. You won’t be pushing security uphill here. More engineers volunteered for our new Security Guild than its first sprint had room for. Building on both companies’ existing security work, the guild is implementing shared product security tools and consistent vulnerability management and incident response processes across Prefect and Dagster. That commitment is helping us stay ahead of AI-accelerated attacks.

You’ll enjoy this role if you like a mix of hands-on work and longer-term improvements, and want a meaningful say in how our IT and compliance programs run.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN

 - Run day-to-day compliance. Keep SOC 2 controls, evidence collection, access reviews, policy acknowledgments and training on track. Work directly with auditors and control owners, and follow findings through to resolution.

 - Help consolidate our compliance programs. With our team lead and consultant, choose a GRC platform and set up both programs. Help adapt control descriptions across environments and design activities that minimize manual work.

 - Own corporate IT. Run Google Workspace and our SaaS apps, handle onboarding and offboarding with People Operations, and manage our Mac fleet in Rippling. Help employees with laptop and access issues, and improve the setup as you learn where people get stuck.

 - Improve access management. Work with our identity partner on how access is requested, approved, granted and removed. Own the daily processes and keep them documented.

 - Protect corporate systems. Manage macOS and application updates, investigate endpoint alerts, and track vulnerabilities through remediation. Verify fixes and participate in phishing and other corporate incident response with our team lead.

 - Automate repetitive work. Use scripts, APIs, workflow tools or AI to reduce manual IT and compliance tasks and make common requests self-service.

Recently completed projects include consolidating Mac device management into Rippling, running access reviews that support both SOC 2 programs, and working with teams to assign tool owners and retire duplicates.




WHERE THE ROLE CAN GROW

We’re building the Security & Systems function for the combined company, and this role will help shape it. Starting with ownership of day-to-day IT and compliance, you can grow toward broader security operations and engineering—including vulnerability management, corporate incident response, and corporate security engineering—or toward risk management and AI governance. The direction will depend on your strengths, interests, and the company’s needs, with opportunities to take on more program ownership and planning as the function develops.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

We’re looking for hands-on IT and compliance experience, practical technical judgment, and the ability to take ownership. Your experience may be deeper in one area, but you should be comfortable across both.

 - You’ve owned recurring SOC 2 activities and worked directly with external auditors, or bring auditing experience. You understand how controls work, what evidence demonstrates they’re operating, and how to adapt them across systems and teams.

 - You’ve administered and secured corporate IT systems, including account management, onboarding/ offboarding and Macs managed through an MDM. You’re comfortable with patching, endpoint alerts, remediation tracking, phishing or suspicious account activity, and helping employees troubleshoot problems.

 - You’re comfortable automating recurring tasks with scripts, APIs, workflow tools or AI, and can explain something you’ve built. A small, useful improvement is a good example.

 - You drive work across teams: establish owners and deadlines, work through blockers, and follow through until tasks are completed and documented. You know when to resolve something yourself and when to escalate.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with Google Workspace, Rippling, or a GRC platform such as Vanta, Drata or Thoropass.

 - Familiarity with SSO, SCIM provisioning or other ways to automate account access.

 - Experience helping implement or migrate an IT or compliance system, or improving a process that involved several teams.




WHO THIS ROLE IS NOT FOR

 - You’re looking to leave hands-on IT support behind. Helping someone with a laptop or access problem is part of the job, alongside larger projects and automation work.

 - You need a settled, fully documented environment from day one. We’re still bringing two companies’ systems together, and you’ll help work out how the combined setup should run.




WHAT YOU'LL GET IN RETURN:

Base Salary Ranges:

 - San Francisco Bay Area and NYC metro: $165,000 - $219,000

 - Washington, D.C., Boston, LA metro and Seattle: $150,000 - $194,000

 - Denver, Chicago, Atlanta and all other US metros: $149,000 - $193,000

Actual base salary within each range depends on the candidate's location, experience, and qualifications. Equity and benefits are not included in the range above. Your recruiter can share more about the salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process.

Perks and Benefits:

 - Remote-first team with flexible-first culture

 - Equity Stock Options

 - 401(k) with 5% company match (vests immediately!)

 - Unlimited PTO

 - Medical, Dental and Vision insurance

 - Generous Parental Leave

 - Life Insurance and Disability benefits

 - $800/month remote work stipend

And that's just the start — for more info check out our benefits and perks on our careers page.


BELONGINGNESS AT PREFECT:


Belongingness at Prefect is our commitment to ensuring mutual power, access, and opportunity among all groups and individuals who make up our community. We operationalize belongingness through actions large and small on a daily basis, but always with the goal that all groups and individuals can contribute as their most authentic self to the evolution of our product, our team, and our community.

Belongingness is also our commitment to bridge with individuals or groups not yet established in our community, acknowledge differences in a way that affirms distinct identities, and allows for a new, more expansive group identity to form.



EQUAL OPPORTUNITY AT PREFECT:

Prefect is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from people of all backgrounds. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, religion, color, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation and gender identity/expression), national origin, disability or any other status protected under applicable federal, state, or local laws.


Delaney is a real live person (👋🏻) and is looking forward to learning more about you through your application.

 - Own the platform that schedules and runs training, evaluation, and reinforcement-learning jobs on Kubernetes: who gets capacity, what happens when a job fails, and how a researcher finds out whether the platform caused it.

 - Run a job platform, batch system, or Kubernetes controllers in production. Scheduling, queues, and multi-tenant fairness are central to this work.

 - Shown distributed systems judgment: retries, partial failure, and knowing what not to automate.

 - Worked on ML training workflows, RL sandboxes, container networking (CNI), or checkpoint storage at scale. Direct GPU-cluster experience is a plus.

 - Written software in Python or Go. You would rather extend a solid open-source project than rebuild it.

 - Worked with researchers, ML engineers, or another team whose goals were not identical to yours.

 - Found a bottleneck, proposed a fix, and driven it in a fast-moving environment.

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. 


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.
